name: Question 4
worked_solution:
Recall that a linear congruence $ax≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ has a unique solution modulo $n$ if and only if $\text{gcd}(a,n)=1.$

In the given congruence, we have $a=6$ and $n=25$, and

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(6,25)=1.
$$

So, our congruence does indeed have a unique solution.

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $6\,(\text{mod}\,25).$ To find the inverse of $6\,(\text{mod}\,25)$, we compute the exponents of $6\,(\text{mod}\,25)$ until we get a result of $1\,(\text{mod}\,25):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{6}^{2} & ≡36≡25+11≡11 &  & (\text{mod}\,25) \\ {6}^{3} & ≡11\cdot 6≡66≡2\cdot 25+16≡16 &  & (\text{mod}\,25) \\ {6}^{4} & ≡16\cdot 6≡96≡3\cdot 25+21≡21 &  & (\text{mod}\,25) \\ {6}^{5} & ≡21\cdot 6≡126≡5\cdot 25+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,25)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $21\cdot 6≡1\,(\text{mod}\,25),$ which means that $21$ is the multiplicative inverse of $6$ (modulo $25$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our congruence by $21,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}6x & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,25) \\ 21\cdot 6x & ≡21\cdot 3 &  & (\text{mod}\,25) \\ (21\cdot 6)x & ≡63 &  & (\text{mod}\,25) \\ 1\cdot x & ≡2\cdot 25+13 &  & (\text{mod}\,25) \\ x & ≡13 &  & (\text{mod}\,25)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡13\,(\text{mod}\,25).$

Recall that a linear congruence ax≡b(modn) has a unique solution modulo n if and only if gcd(a,n)=1.

In the given congruence, we have a=6 and n=25, and gcd(a,n)=gcd(6,25)=1. So, our congruence does indeed have a unique solution.

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of 6(mod25). To find the inverse of 6(mod25), we compute the exponents of 6(mod25) until we get a result of 1(mod25):

62≡36≡25+11≡11(mod25)63≡11⋅6≡66≡2⋅25+16≡16(mod25)64≡16⋅6≡96≡3⋅25+21≡21(mod25)65≡21⋅6≡126≡5⋅25+1≡1(mod25)

So, 21⋅6≡1(mod25), which means that 21 is the multiplicative inverse of 6 (modulo 25).

Now, multiplying both sides of our congruence by 21, we get the following:

6x≡3(mod25)21⋅6x≡21⋅3(mod25)(21⋅6)x≡63(mod25)1⋅x≡2⋅25+13(mod25)x≡13(mod25)

Therefore, the solution is x≡13(mod25).
